summary: N. Lakshminarayana Rao worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and was Special Officer (Epigraphy) for the Government of India in 1956.

N. P. Chakravarti (1893–1956), an Indologist and archaeologist, studied at Calcutta, Paris, Berlin, and Cambridge (PhD). He held posts at Calcutta, Berlin, and Sorbonne, and served as Director General of Archaeology in India (1948–1950) among multiple ASI appointments.
N. R. Bhatt (1920–2009) was an Indologist. He held positions at the French Institute of Pondicherry and served as a member of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 1966).

N. S. Ramachandra Murthy is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He was an Epigraphy Assistant in the Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums (attested 1981) and retired as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Sri Venkateswara University.

N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya (1928–2017) was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Vice Chancellor of Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha from 1989 to 1994 and worked as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry from around 1989 to 2017.

N. Veezhinathan, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, earned his PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under doctoral supervisor A. Sankaran. He held positions at Deccan College (1960–1963) and the University of Madras from 1964.

N. Venkataramanayya (1891–1976), who studied under Ferrand Edward Corley, worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Reader in Indian History at the University of Madras (attested 1957) and Deputy Director for Epigraphy for Andhra Pradesh.

Nae Ionescu (1890–1940) worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Bucharest (around 1909–1912), the University of Göttingen, and the University of Munich, before holding a post at the University of Bucharest from around 1919 to 1940.
Nagin J. Shah (born 1931) is an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Acting Director of the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology around 1968, succeeding Dalsukh Malvania.

Nalinaksha Dutt (1894–1973) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned doctorates from Calcutta and London and served as Head of Pali at Calcutta (c. 1920–1958) and President of The Asiatic Society (1959–1961).

Nalini Balbir (born 1955) is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Colette Caillat. She held posts at the CNRS (1982–1988), Sorbonne Nouvelle University (from 1988), the University of Paris, and École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2000).

Nalini Devdas specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. Supervised by Leslie Orr, she completed her PhD at Concordia University (attested 2004) and held an attested post at Carleton University in 2004.

Nam-lin Hur works in Japanology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at Princeton under Helen Hardacre, later serving as professor of Japanese history and religious culture at UBC.

Naman P. Ahuja is an Indologist and art historian who earned his doctorate from SOAS University of London. He was appointed Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

Namgyal Rinpoche (1931–2003) studied at Jarvis Baptist Seminary, the University of Michigan, and under various traditional teachers in Buddhist and religious studies. He founded the Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre (1965) and the Dharma Centre of Canada (1966).

Namio Egami (1906–2002), a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied at the University of Tokyo (around 1927–1930). He taught at the University of Tokyo (c. 1948–1967) and directed the Ancient Orient Museum (c. 1978–2002).
Namita Das is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University under the doctoral supervision of Sibnath Sarma (attested 2012).

Namkhai Norbu (1938–2018), a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at Derge Gonchen, Kuse Serjong, and Khamdre Shedra. He taught at Southwest Minzu University, the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East, and Naples (1962–1992).
Nancy Grace Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed graduate study at Columbia University and earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley.

Nancy Hock, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD in 1987 from the University of California, Berkeley, under Joanna Gottfried Williams. She held an attested post at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco in 1987.
